name: Harava identification database
description: Harava's own rules for radios that Fieldwatch's signatures leave unidentified. Rules are tried in order; the first that matches wins. A rule only changes the layer of a radio that Fieldwatch did not identify; for the others it adds the 'Identified as' text. Company names come from bt_assigned_numbers.json (Bluetooth SIG).

match (all given conditions must hold).name_regex: regular expression on the advertised name (case-insensitive)
match (all given conditions must hold).mfg: Bluetooth company ID of the manufacturer data, 4 hex digits, e.g. 004C = Apple
match (all given conditions must hold).mfg_data_prefix: hex the manufacturer data (after the company ID) starts with
match (all given conditions must hold).ad_type: advertising data type in the raw advertisement, 2 hex digits, e.g. 2B = Mesh Beacon
match (all given conditions must hold).ad_data_prefix: hex the data of that AD structure starts with
match (all given conditions must hold).ad_data_regex: regular expression on the hex (upper case) of the data of that AD structure, for patterns a prefix cannot tell
match (all given conditions must hold).service_data_regex: regular expression on the hex of the Service Data of service_data_uuid
match (all given conditions must hold).service_data_uuid: 16-bit UUID of Service Data, 4 hex digits
match (all given conditions must hold).service_uuid_any: list of 16-bit service UUIDs; one of them must be advertised
match (all given conditions must hold).uuid128_any: list of 128-bit service UUIDs (8-4-4-4-12); one of them must be advertised

schema.group: how to tell that several rotating addresses are the same device: take bytes [from, to) of the AD structure ad_type, of the manufacturer data (source = mfg) or of the service data of uuid (source = service_data). key (optional) names the group; rules with the same key join the same devices, e.g. two kinds of advert from one Mesh device
schema.confidence: high = the protocol says so; medium = typical, well known; low = a likely guess
schema.name_from_group: a nameless address that belongs to a group whose other addresses tell a name is identified again with that name, so e.g. the nameless Mesh beacons of a "Charge" device also become EV charging points

rules.name: Printer (Wi-Fi Direct)
rules.note: A printer's own Wi-Fi Direct network for printing without a router.

rules.name: Philips Hue lamp
rules.note: Advertises Signify's Hue Bluetooth service (FE0F). Hue lamps keep it on even when they have no name or a room name.

rules.name: Signify (Philips / WiZ) lighting
rules.note: Advertises a Bluetooth service number registered to Signify, the maker of Philips Hue and WiZ lights.

rules.name: Signify (Philips / WiZ) lighting
rules.note: Manufacturer data of Signify Netherlands B.V. (company 060F), the maker of Philips Hue and WiZ lights.

rules.name: EV charging point (DEFA?)
rules.note: A Bluetooth Mesh device named "Charge" that is waiting to be set up. Seen in numbers around a shared EV charging system of a housing company (most likely DEFA chargers, which are configured over Bluetooth); they advertise all day like mains-powered equipment. The maker is not confirmed by a public source, hence the question mark.

rules.name: EV charging point (DEFA?)
rules.note: A Bluetooth Mesh device waiting to be set up, whose device UUID has the form of the charge points named "Charge" (eight random bytes, then 80 and seven zero bytes). It did not tell its name in this data; every device of this form whose name was heard later was a charge point. Another product built on the same radio module could look the same.

rules.name: EcoFlow power station
rules.note: EcoFlow names its devices EF-<model><serial>, e.g. EF-R3P… for a River 3 Plus.

rules.name: Oras smart faucet or shower
rules.note: Oras (Finland) makes Bluetooth faucets and showers.

rules.name: Windows PC
rules.note: Advertises the 128-bit service 3E1D50CD-7E3E-427D-8E1C-B78AA87FE624. Every radio with this service that told a name had a Windows PC name, so it is a Windows service shared by many PCs, not a fingerprint of one PC. Its public meaning is not documented.

rules.name: Bluetooth Mesh device, not set up
rules.note: An Unprovisioned Device Beacon: a smart lamp, plug or switch waiting to be added to a Bluetooth Mesh network. It changes its address often but keeps the same device UUID, so Harava can tell the addresses of one device apart from the others.

rules.name: Bluetooth Mesh network node
rules.note: A Secure Network Beacon of a set-up Bluetooth Mesh network (smart lighting and the like). The group is the network, not one device.

rules.name: Bluetooth Mesh device, not set up
rules.note: Mesh Provisioning service (1827): a device waiting to be added to a Bluetooth Mesh network, offering a phone a connection for the setup. Its service data carries the same device UUID as its Unprovisioned Device Beacons, so Harava joins both kinds of advert into one device.

rules.name: Bluetooth Mesh device, set up
rules.note: Mesh Proxy service (1828): a device that is already in a Bluetooth Mesh network and lets a phone connect to it.

rules.name: LE Audio device (earbuds, headphones or hearing aid)
rules.note: Bluetooth LE Audio services (audio stream control, broadcast scan, volume, microphone, hearing access …).

rules.name: AirPods or Beats
rules.note: Apple Proximity Pairing message.

rules.name: iPhone, iPad, Mac or Apple Watch
rules.note: Apple Nearby Info message, sent all the time by Apple devices.

rules.name: Apple device (Nearby Action: setup or Wi-Fi sharing)
Apple TV, HomePod or AirPlay speaker
Apple device looking for a hotspot
Apple device
rules.note: An Apple message type that Harava does not know yet (for example 0x16 or 0x1C); most such messages come from iPhones, iPads and Macs.

rules.name: Samsung Galaxy device (phone, tablet, PC or watch)
rules.note: Samsung's 0x42 message, sent by Galaxy devices for SmartThings and nearby sharing.

rules.name: Windows device
rules.note: Microsoft manufacturer data (Swift Pair / connected devices).

rules.name: Oral-B electric toothbrush
rules.note: Company ID 0x00DC is Procter & Gamble, the owner of Oral-B; their Bluetooth toothbrushes advertise with it.

rules.name: BEHA heater
rules.note: Seen with the text 'Beha heater' in its manufacturer data.

rules.name: Google / Android device (service FEF3)
rules.note: Service data with Google's member UUID FEF3. Google does not document it; most such advertisers are Android phones and Google devices nearby, rotating their address.

rules.name: Google / Android device (service FCF1)
rules.note: Service data with Google's member UUID FCF1 (registered 2022). Not documented; seen from Android devices.
